title: Linearization, differentials, and approximation error
section: Linear Approximations Using Differentials ▷ Local approximation
terms: linear approximation; linearization; differential approximation; relative error; tangent approximation.

question.text:

solution.text:
dy/y = (−3/2)dx/x. Multiplying 0.004 by −3/2 gives −0.006, or a 0.6% underestimate.

question.text:
For f(x) = log x, let L be the linearization at x = 1. Which bound holds for |f(1.1) − L(1.1)|?
(A) At most 1/200 (B) Greater than 1/20
(C) At least 1/10 (D) Exactly 1/100
(E) Exactly zero

solution.text:
′′ 2 2
On [1, 1.1], |f (x)| = 1/x ≤ 1. Taylor’s bound is (1/2)(0.1) = 1/200; concavity also shows
the tangent approximation lies above the logarithm.
